description: Data + types foundation for alerts: I-prefixed interfaces in src/types/index.ts, the Next.js 16 alerts route handler (typed mock IAlertState, 15-min revalidate, Filipino try/catch fallback), and the offline-first useAlerts client hook with localStorage cache. This feature is a prerequisite for FEAT-002 (the UI consumes these types, the route, and the hook).
steps: Edit src/types/index.ts: replace the `export {}` placeholder with exported I-prefixed interfaces (additive, keep the file otherwise minimal since a concurrent branch also edits it): `IHazardAlert { signalLevel: 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5; typhoonName: string; affectedAreas: string[]; timestamp: string; severity: "advisory" | "warning" | "emergency" }`, `IEvacuationCenter { name: string; distance: string; capacity: string; directionsUrl: string }`, `IHotline { label: string; number: string; tel: string }`, `IAlertState { hasActiveHazard: boolean; alert: IHazardAlert | null; evacuationCenters: IEvacuationCenter[]; hotlines: IHotline[]; source: string; fetchedAt: string }`.

Create src/app/api/alerts/route.ts following node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/route.md: add `export const revalidate = 900;` (static literal — required for the 15-min cache under the no-Cache-Components model) and a named `export async function GET()`. Inside a try/catch, build a well-typed mock IAlertState (import the types from `@/types`): one active sample typhoon (signalLevel 3, a typhoonName, affectedAreas incl. a CALABARZON area, ISO timestamp, severity "warning"), hasActiveHazard true, 1-2 IEvacuationCenter entries, hotlines [911, Philippine Red Cross 143, NDRRMC (02) 8911-1406 / 911-5061] as IHotline, source "mock", fetchedAt new Date().toISOString(). Return Response.json(state). In catch, return Response.json of a safe fallback IAlertState (hasActiveHazard false, alert null, empty centers, same hotlines, source "fallback") with status 200 so the client never breaks. Structure the code so a real NDRRMC/PAGASA fetch (with `next: { revalidate: 900 }`) can replace the mock. No console.log. Leave the sibling placeholder src/app/api/alerts/index.ts untouched.

Create src/hooks/useAlerts.ts: a client hook (`"use client"`) `export function useAlerts()` returning `{ state: IAlertState | null; loading: boolean; error: string | null; refetch: () => void }`. On mount and on refetch, fetch("/api/alerts"); on ok, parse JSON as IAlertState, set state, and write to localStorage key `klimaguard:lastAlertState` as `{ state, cachedAt: Date.now() }`. On fetch failure or non-ok, read that localStorage key and use the cached state if present, and set a Filipino error string (e.g. "Hindi makakonekta. Ipinapakita ang huling nalamang alerto."). 15-min freshness convention: treat cachedAt older than 900000ms as stale (still show it offline, but allow refetch). Guard all localStorage access with typeof window checks and try/catch. No `any`, no console.log.
Edit src/hooks/index.ts: replace `export {}` with `export * from "./useAlerts";` (additive barrel update).
acceptance_criteria: src/types/index.ts exports IHazardAlert, IEvacuationCenter, IHotline, IAlertState with the exact shapes above and no `any`.
GET /api/alerts returns JSON conforming to IAlertState with source "mock" on success; the handler has `export const revalidate = 900` and cannot throw a 500 (catch returns a 200 fallback).
useAlerts is exported from the hooks barrel and compiles; it caches to and restores from localStorage and exposes loading/error/refetch.
`npm run lint` and `npm run build` succeed from the worktree with no errors.
verification: Optional manual: npm run dev then GET http://localhost:3000/api/alerts returns IAlertState JSON (do not leave dev running as a blocking task).
